newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dassault row with France near end - Belgian PM.
newsitem.headline: Dassault row with France near end - Belgian PM.

text.p: Belgium's row with France over secret French documents needed for its Dassault bribery probe should be resolved on Thursday, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said.

"In the Dassault affair I have learnt that the problem will be sorted out tomorrow," Dehaene said during a joint news conference with French President Jacques Chirac, who began an official visit to Brussels on Wednesday.

The documents, wanted for an inquiry involving French warplane maker Dassault Aviation, focus in a long-running dispute which broke when France's former centre-right government refused to hand them over despite Belgian insistence.
Chirac confirmed that documents would be sent on Thursday.

"All the transmissible documents will be sent tomorrow. The only documents not transmitted are those touching on French security interests, which are of no interest to Belgium," he told the same news conference.

Belgian police are investigating allegations that the Dassault company paid 600 million Belgian francs ($17 million) to Belgian political parties to secure a contract to fit air defence systems to Belgian F-16 jets in the late 1980s.
